title: Truncation and heart theorem for t-admissible condensed coefficients
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$. Assume that $R$ is regular coherent, meaning that every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented and every finitely presented $R$-module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projective $R$-modules, and that $R\to\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$ is flat for every extremally disconnected profinite set $S$ (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space in which the closure of every open set is open). These two assumptions are the meaning of t-admissibility here.

Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In the ambient derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_X[0]$. Let $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(X,\Lambda)$ denote its full subcategory of dualizable objects, where dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation with the two triangle identities.

The ambient standard truncation functors $\tau^{\le n}$ and $\tau^{\ge n}$ preserve $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(X,\Lambda)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. They define the restriction of the ambient standard t-structure to this subcategory. Its heart is exactly the sheaves pro-etale locally isomorphic to
$$\Lambda_X\otimes_{\underline R}\underline N$$
for finitely presented $R$-modules $N$; the module $N$ may depend on the member of the cover. Here $\underline R$ and $\underline N$ are constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and the tensor uses the canonical constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_X$. In particular every cohomology sheaf of a dualizable object has this local form.
